items.title: Charles Calello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2025
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions Roger Williams in a list of artists from the late '50s/early '60s; INTERVIEWEE does not mention Roger Williams in their response.

ctx.x: Yeah well there were a couple of them that were written that way too.

What possessed you – I’m wondering if there was an Aha! moment or – because I was looking at the Top 10 list of various years. And in the late ‘50s, early ‘60s there was such a variety of things. In 1949 you had “Bird with Strings” and then 1950 the “Third Man Theme,” and Nat King Cole, Roger Williams, “Rock Around the Clock.” Did some particular tune or style make a big impression on you?

That’s a good question because prior to me going and playing in the bar when I was 15, I remember over the summer I started to listen more closely to the radio. And I heard The Four Freshman sing “Day by Day.” And I went and I bought the record. And also I heard Johnny Ray sing “Cry” and “The Little White Cloud that Cried.” In fact I actually wrote an arrangement that I really, really liked for Ronnie Milsap with a big band and strings of the song “Cry” which actually became, for a while it was like a favorite,…
